references.text: Describes the plague of boils in Egypt, where Moses and Aaron cast soot that turned into boils on the Egyptians and their livestock—the same 'שְׁחִין מִצְרַיִם' (boils of Egypt) mentioned in Deuteronomy 28:27
God promises not to lay any of Egypt's diseases upon Israel if they are obedient—contrasting with the curse in Deuteronomy 28:27 that threatens boils from Egypt for disobedience
Laws concerning skin diseases and boils (שְׁחִין) that priests must examine—the same type of disease mentioned as a curse
Promise that the Lord will keep all sickness away and not lay any of Egypt's evil diseases upon Israel—opposite to the curse in 28:27
The Philistines were struck with boils (עֳפָלִים/טְחֹרִים) when they had the ark of the covenant—the same plague mentioned in the curse
The Philistines made golden images of their boils as a guilt offering—showing the severity of the plagues mentioned in Deuteronomy 28:27
Job was struck with painful boils (שְׁחִין) from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head—the same type of affliction described in the curse
